art.title: The Fall of Man [middle panel]
art.why: Goltzius is used; this is the moment of choice: the woman holds a bitten apple, the serpent coiled above her, in a forest of fruit trees.

art.title: Vanitas Still Life
art.why: Skull, roses full-blown and in bud, half-run hourglass, soap bubbles, insects on the flowers: good things passing and spoiling, for evil as lack, not thing. The description shows no rot as such; describe only what it lists.

art.title: Saint Jerome Penitent [right panel]
art.why: A man kneeling, beating his chest with a rock, looking up: 'What a wretched man I am!' (Romans 7:24). Grisaille panel.

art.title: Waterloo Bridge, London, at Dusk
art.why: Jekyll's London at nightfall, a bridge half dissolved in haze: the city where a man could be two men. Painted 1904, close to Stevenson's time.

Every NGA Adam and Eve is already in art.json and in journeys (goltzius-fall, west-expulsion, domenichino-rebuke, giovanni-expulsion), and the one free work is used for s1. Option for the reviewer: reuse west-expulsion (in in-the-beginning) only if the owner allows a repeat.

art.title: Saint George and the Dragon
art.why: No Archangel Michael at NGA. Evil overcome: the dragon pinned and defeated, the woman watching. Flag: a fight, where Romans 12:21 speaks of overcoming evil with good; the lecture should name the difference.

music.why: Psalm 51 sung: the prayer of a man who did evil and asked for a clean heart, the journey's learn piece.
